## Teaching points

1. Ottawa ankle rules: ankle X-ray only if malleolar-zone pain AND bony tenderness at the posterior edge/tip of either malleolus (distal 6 cm) OR inability to bear weight both immediately and in the ED (4 steps).
2. Foot X-ray only if midfoot pain AND tenderness at the base of the 5th metatarsal or the navicular, OR inability to bear weight.
3. Acute lateral ankle sprains: functional treatment (brace, early weight-bearing, exercise therapy) beats rigid immobilization; NSAIDs are effective for pain. MRI adds nothing acutely.
4. A delayed physical exam (4–5 days) is more accurate for ligament rupture (anterior drawer) once swelling settles.
5. Prior authorization applies to scheduled advanced imaging, never to emergency care — and knowing the criteria saves everyone a phone call.

1. Stiell IG, et al. Implementation of the Ottawa ankle rules. JAMA. 1994;271:827–832.
2. Bachmann LM, et al. Accuracy of Ottawa ankle rules to exclude fractures of the ankle and mid-foot: systematic review. BMJ. 2003;326:417.
3. Vuurberg G, et al. Diagnosis, treatment and prevention of ankle sprains: update of an evidence-based clinical guideline. Br J Sports Med. 2018;52:956.
